Northbridge weighs a one-semester measles clinic inside public high schools. Most speakers ask for the protocol and have not picked a side.

In April 2026 the “Northbridge Health Board” sent a draft to the “Northbridge School District”. The draft would park a clinic in each public high school for one semester. “Mara Ellison”, speaking for the board, said the text is a consultation paper. “Owen Briggs”, principal of “Northbridge Central High”, said his staff want the consent form before commenting. “Helen Cho” and “Priya Nandak”, both clinic physicians named in the draft, have not issued a joint letter.

“Jonah Hale” of the “Northbridge Parents Forum” published a survey in which most replies were “need more detail”. “Ruth Adler”, chair of the “Northbridge Teachers Circle”, said members are split between waiting and asking questions, not between yes and no. “Evan Moss” at the “Northbridge Civic Register” reported that the hearing questions were about queues, privacy, and catch-up lessons. “Lila Chen”, a nurse lead at “Harbor Lane Clinic”, said she would staff the room if the district asks, and stopped there. “Samuel Ortiz”, counsel for the “Northbridge Student Council”, said the council has not voted.

“June Park” of the “Family Cooperative” told the hearing she is undecided until the opt-out line is printed in full.

“Ada Quinn”, “Noah Patel”, “Iris Berg”, “Cole Tran”, “Mina Shah”, and “Paul Ibarra” each sent a one-line note asking for the consent form. “Lane Health Board” and “Civic Register” reprinted those notes without a yes or a no. No large campaign for or against the clinic has started.
